## Answer: no, the repo ships zero agent-facing context

The scan flags it explicitly — `crime_00011`, **Missing Agent Context**, medium severity, confidence 0.90, `agent_risk` 0.47. That puts it 11th out of 92 findings by aggregate risk, above every single one of the 40-odd God Functions below it.

The evidence is a clean sweep:

- no `AGENTS.md` at root
- no `CLAUDE.md` at root
- no `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- no `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- `package.json` declares bins `tsup`, `tsup-node` — so the repo *is* a published tool, and an agent has no way to discover how to build or test it

Coverage confirms there's no accidental substitute: 52 files scanned, exactly 3 markdown files, all universal-only. Whatever those are (README/CHANGELOG-shaped), none of them registered as agent instructions.

One caveat on reading the JSON: the finding is anchored to `assets/cjs_shims.js`. That's a repo-level fact wearing an arbitrary file path — don't go looking for the problem in that file.

## Why this matters for your first PR specifically

Missing agent context is only a paperwork problem in a repo where mistakes are cheap. This isn't one, and the rest of the same scan says why:

**The blast radius is concentrated in four files an agent has no reason to be careful about.** `src/utils.ts` has 18 direct importers and 29 transitive (`crime_00039`) and is a 424-line God File (`crime_00047`). `src/plugin.ts`: fan-in 10, 29 transitive. `src/log.ts`: fan-in 9, 30 transitive — the widest reach in the repo. `src/index.ts` pulls in 17 modules and holds a 293-line `build()`. Nothing in the repo tells an agent "these are load-bearing"; it has to infer that by reading the import graph, which it usually won't.

**The test suite will not catch the mistake.** This is the sharp edge. 12 tests contain zero assertions (`crime_00055`–`crime_00066`) — including `custom tsconfig`, `removeNodeProtocol works on shims`, and five `experimentalDts` config tests. Another 14 rely only on weak matchers (`crime_00077`–`crime_00090`). An agent that runs the suite, sees green, and reports "verified" is reporting the exit code of a build, not protected behaviour. That's the false-confidence loop an AGENTS.md exists to break.

**Two local conventions look like bugs and will get "fixed."** All three build runners catch, log a message, and drop the error (`crime_00044` api-extractor:197, `crime_00045` tsc:215, `crime_00051` rollup:187 — each 0.66 confidence, each with the same "log call omits the error value" delta). And `jsoncParse` in `src/utils.ts:135` returns `{}` on any parse failure with no catch binding at all. Whether those are deliberate CLI ergonomics or genuine gaps is a decision the repo has made and not written down. An agent will pick one answer at random.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector accepts any one of the four surfaces. `AGENTS.md` at root is the right pick — it's tool-agnostic and Claude Code reads it too, so you don't need a parallel `CLAUDE.md`.

I've left the command block with `<!-- verify -->` markers: the scan tells me the bins are `tsup` and `tsup-node`, but it doesn't expose `package.json` scripts or the package manager, so fill those from the manifest rather than trusting my guess.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Build tool that compiles TS/JS via esbuild, with dts emitted through
rollup / tsc / api-extractor. Published bins: `tsup`, `tsup-node`.

## Commands
<!-- verify against package.json scripts before relying on these -->
- Install: `pnpm install`
- Build:   `pnpm build`
- Test:    `pnpm test`
- Single:  `pnpm test -- test/index.test.ts`

## Test signal is weaker than it looks

A green run is not proof. 12 tests in `test/` have no assertions at all
and ~14 more only assert weakly. Notably unprotected: `custom tsconfig`,
`removeNodeProtocol works on shims`, and the `experimentalDts` config
variants.

If you change behaviour, add a real assertion for it. Do not treat a
passing suite as verification.

## Load-bearing files — read importers before restructuring

| File                 | Reach                        |
|----------------------|------------------------------|
| `src/utils.ts`       | 18 direct / 29 transitive    |
| `src/plugin.ts`      | 10 direct / 29 transitive    |
| `src/log.ts`         |  9 direct / 30 transitive    |
| `src/index.ts`       | imports 17 modules           |
| `src/esbuild/index.ts` | imports 11 modules         |

Prefer additive changes here. `src/utils.ts` (424 lines) and
`src/index.ts` (459 lines) are known-large; splitting them is a
deliberate project decision, not a drive-by cleanup.

## Conventions that are intentional
<!-- confirm each with a maintainer, then delete this comment -->

- Build runners (`api-extractor.ts`, `tsc.ts`, `rollup.ts`) catch, log,
  and swallow. Do not convert these to rethrows as an incidental fix.
- `jsoncParse` (`src/utils.ts`) returns `{}` on parse failure by design.
- Plugin `setup()` functions return several object shapes on purpose —
  that's the esbuild/rollup plugin contract, not a bug.

## Before you open a PR

- Scope the diff to the change you were asked for.
- If you touched a file in the table above, say so in the description.
- If you changed a swallowed-error site or a plugin return shape, flag
  it — those need a human decision.
```

That's ~50 lines and clears `crime_00011` outright. The three `<!-- verify -->` / `<!-- confirm -->` markers are the parts I inferred from finding evidence rather than read from source — worth ten minutes with the manifest and a maintainer before you commit it, otherwise you've replaced "no context" with "confidently wrong context," which is worse.
